items.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
items.scope: Defines what governance outcomes to achieve. The SRF answers who owns each component.

items.name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
items.scope: Defines which regulatory obligations apply by risk tier (Unacceptable / High / Limited / Minimal). Applies to providers and deployers placing AI systems on the EU market.
items.vertical_scope_note: Absent from the public-sector and defense schemas by design, not by omission. Those two schemas declare a US-only scope (federal civilian agencies and DoD with the defense industrial base), and Article 2(3) excludes AI used exclusively for military, defence, or national security purposes.

items.name: ISO/IEC 42001 — AI Management Systems
items.scope: Defines how to manage an AI management system. Certifiable standard. The SRF layer model maps directly into its organizational and technical controls.
items.vertical_scope_note: A horizontal management-system standard cited only by manufacturing. The clause-level mapping is withheld on purpose: the standard text is paywalled, so manufacturing cites it at edition level (decision 2026-07-05) rather than publishing clause numbers nobody can check. Copying edition-level citations into the other five schemas would add governed_by edges that carry no clause evidence, so the declared list stays at what is actually cited. Same reasoning holds for IEC 62443 and IEC 61508, which are also OT-specific by subject.

items.name: ISO/IEC 22989 — AI Concepts and Terminology
items.scope: Defines the eight AI stakeholder roles (§5.19) that map directly to the CoSAI SRF personas.

items.name: NIST AI 600-1 — AI RMF: Generative AI Profile
items.scope: Companion profile to the NIST AI RMF (AI 100-1) that identifies 12 risk categories unique or exacerbated by generative AI and maps over 200 suggested actions to the RMF's Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage functions. It supplements, and does not replace, the base AI RMF. In the SRF this is the substantive genAI mapping target where a broad regulation (e.g. SR 26-2, which places generative AI out of scope) leaves genAI controls unaddressed; its security-control counterpart is the forthcoming COSAiS overlay NISTIR 8605B (Generative AI).

items.name: NISTIR 8605A — Control Overlays for Securing AI Systems: Using and Fine-Tuning Predictive AI
items.scope: SP 800-53 control overlays tailoring the 800-53B moderate baseline (FIPS 199 moderate) for AI systems. Part of the COSAiS series: NISTIR 8605 (Overview and Methodology), 8605A (Predictive AI, this entry), 8605B (Generative AI), 8605C (AI Developers), 8605D (Agentic AI, single and multi-agent). Overlays are built by mapping the NIST AI 100-2e2025 adversarial ML taxonomy (attack IDs such as NIST AML.011) to 800-53 controls, tailored across AI lifecycle phases (Model Training / Deployment / Maintenance / Continuous). Annotated outline issued for Cyber AI Profile Workshop #2 (Jan 14, 2026); 8605 and 8605A initial public drafts expected Q3 FY2026, series finalized 2027. Subject to change.

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Control Overlays for Securing AI Systems: Using and Fine-Tuning Predictive AI — Annotated Outline for Cyber AI Profile Workshop #2
references.note: Draft content to be incorporated into NISTIR 8605 and 8605A. Comment deadline Feb 13, 2026.

items.vertical_scope_note: Author-declared scope, no evidence edge. The public-sector schema carries a cosais key on every control, but each value is a TBD placeholder because the overlays were still pre-draft (annotated outline only) when the schema was written, and inventing overlay IDs was rejected. The generator skips placeholders, so the evidence path stays empty until the initial public drafts land and real overlay IDs replace the placeholders.

items.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
items.scope: Voluntary framework for managing cybersecurity risk across six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. CSF 2.0 added Govern as a new function and expanded scope beyond critical infrastructure. AI systems fall under CSF Govern and Identify functions primarily at L1 and L3.

items.name: OWASP LLM Top 10
items.scope: Ten most critical security risks for LLM-powered applications. Maps to L3 (application guardrails) and L4 (platform-level mitigations).

items.name: CSA AI Controls Matrix
items.scope: 243 controls across 18 domains with crosswalks to EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI 600-1, and BSI AI C4. Ownership tiers (MP/OSP/AP) map to CoSAI layers.
items.version_note: Catalog pins v1.0.3 on purpose. AICM v1.1 was published 2026-06-22, but the control objective IDs cited by the vertical schemas were verified against 1.0.3. Re-verify every cited objective ID against the newer matrix before bumping this version, since objective numbering can move between releases.

items.name: CIS Critical Security Controls
items.scope: Eighteen prioritized controls and 153 safeguards used as a cyber-hygiene baseline. The 2026 AI Companion Guides interpret account management, secure configuration, audit logging, vulnerability management, and service provider management for LLM systems, agents, and MCP environments. The Controls assume a single organization's estate; the SRF assigns each mapped control to the accountable layer and persona per operating model.

items.name: MITRE ATLAS
items.scope: Adversarial threat landscape for AI-enabled systems. Attack tactics and techniques relevant to L3 application, L4 platform, and L5 model provider layers.

items.name: SR 26-2 — Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management
items.scope: Revised model risk management guidance for financial institutions covering AI/ML systems, superseding the prior SR letter. Risk cascades across layers — model governance obligations span L5 (model provider), L2 (training data), and L1 (deploying organization).

items.name: FDA AI/ML-Based Software as a Medical Device
items.scope: Validation and change-control requirements for AI/ML used in medical devices. Model validation responsibility cascades from L5 (model provider) through L3 (application developer) to L1 (deploying organization).

items.name: General Data Protection Regulation
items.scope: Data protection obligations that intersect AI at the L2 (information / data owner) layer. Relevant to training data, inference data, and automated decision-making (Article 22).

items.name: GAO-21-519SP — AI Accountability Framework for Federal Agencies and Other Entities
items.scope: Published June 2021, before generative AI and foundation models entered mainstream use. Organizes audit questions around four principles, governance, data, performance, and monitoring, but assigns no persona-level accountability: it addresses only three broad audiences (entities, auditors, third-party assessors), not the model provider, platform, application developer, deploying organization, or data owner roles the SRF distinguishes. Retained here as the historical anchor for federal AI audit criteria; OMB M-25-21 and current public-sector obligations build on this lineage rather than superseding it directly.

items.name: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence
items.scope: The first intergovernmental AI standard, adopted by the OECD Council in 2019 and revised in May 2024. Five value-based principles for trustworthy AI plus five recommendations to governments. Principle 1.4 (robustness, security and safety) carries the override, repair, and decommission duty that most national robustness requirements descend from. Soft law: it binds no one directly, but it supplies the vocabulary that the EU AI Act, the NIST AI RMF, and most national strategies reuse, which makes it the natural root when comparing regimes across jurisdictions.

items.name: FINOS AI Governance Framework
items.scope: Open-source AI governance framework for financial services, cataloguing AI risks and mitigations for regulated institutions.

items.name: HIPAA Security Rule
items.body: US Department of Health and Human Services
items.scope: Administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for electronic protected health information. Constrains what clinical AI systems may access, log, and disclose.

items.name: FDA Total Product Life Cycle approach for AI-enabled devices
items.scope: Lifecycle oversight model for AI/ML medical devices spanning premarket review through postmarket performance monitoring.

items.name: FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans for AI-enabled device software
items.scope: Lets a manufacturer pre-authorize specified model changes so retraining does not require a new marketing submission, provided the changes stay inside the agreed protocol.

items.name: ONC HTI-1 Final Rule: Decision Support Interventions
items.scope: Transparency and source-attribute disclosure requirements for predictive decision support interventions in certified health IT.

items.name: IEC 62304: Medical device software lifecycle processes
items.scope: Software lifecycle process requirements for medical device software, including software of unknown provenance.

items.name: ISO 14971: Application of risk management to medical devices
items.scope: Risk management process for medical devices across the product lifecycle.

items.name: NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems by Insurers
items.scope: Model bulletin setting expectations for insurer AI system governance programs. Binding only in states that adopt it, so the same control can be mandatory or advisory depending on the state.

items.name: NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool
items.scope: Examiner-facing tool for evaluating insurer AI governance during market conduct examinations.

items.name: Colorado Division of Insurance Regulation 10-1-1
items.scope: Governance and risk management requirements for life insurers using external consumer data and algorithms in underwriting.

items.name: NYDFS Circular Letter No. 7 (2024): Use of AI Systems in Insurance Underwriting and Pricing
items.body: New York Department of Financial Services
items.scope: Expectations for insurers using AI systems and external consumer data in underwriting and pricing, including unfair discrimination testing.

items.name: OMB M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
items.body: US Office of Management and Budget
items.scope: Federal agency AI governance policy covering use-case inventories, high-impact AI designation, CAIO appointment, and minimum risk management practices.

items.name: OMB M-25-22: Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government
items.body: US Office of Management and Budget
items.scope: Federal AI acquisition policy covering contract terms for performance, transparency, data rights, and vendor lock-in avoidance.

items.name: FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators
items.scope: Machine-verifiable security indicators replacing narrative control descriptions in the FedRAMP 20x authorization model.

items.name: NIST SP 800-171: Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems
items.scope: Security requirements for CUI held in nonfederal systems. The technical baseline underneath CMMC assessment levels.

items.name: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification 2.0
items.scope: Tiered assessment and certification program for defense contractors handling FCI and CUI.

items.name: DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide
items.scope: Security requirements and impact levels (IL2 through IL6) governing DoD use of commercial cloud services.

items.name: DoD Responsible AI Strategy and Implementation Pathway
items.scope: Implementation pathway for the five DoD AI ethical principles: responsible, equitable, traceable, reliable, and governable.

items.name: DoDI 5000.89: Test and Evaluation
items.scope: Test and evaluation policy for defense acquisition programs, the basis for TEVV planning on AI-enabled systems.

items.name: DoDI 5000.90: Cybersecurity for Acquisition Decision Authorities and Program Managers
items.scope: Cybersecurity requirements integrated into defense acquisition, including model transparency documentation.

items.name: NIST Cyber AI Profile
items.scope: In-development CSF 2.0 community profile for cybersecurity of and with AI. Draft status; treat mappings as provisional.

items.name: EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230
items.scope: Safety requirements for machinery placed on the EU market, including machinery with self-evolving behaviour. Applies from January 2027 and interlocks with EU AI Act high-risk obligations.

items.name: IEC 62443: Security for industrial automation and control systems
items.scope: Zone and conduit security model for OT and ICS environments, including AI components deployed at the OT edge.

items.name: IEC 61508: Functional safety of electrical, electronic and programmable electronic safety-related systems
items.scope: Functional safety lifecycle and safety integrity levels for safety-instrumented systems.

items.name: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (UK white paper)
items.scope: Sets a regulator-led, context-specific UK approach to AI rather than a single horizontal AI statute. Five principles (safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, contestability) are delivered through existing sector regulators. Use as the UK comparative anchor until a binding UK AI Act exists.

items.name: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
items.scope: Binding rules for generative AI services offered to the public in China, covering training-data legality, content safety, labeling, and security assessments. Provider and platform duties map primarily to L1 governance and L5 model provision.

items.name: Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services
items.scope: Rules for deep-synthesis and synthetic-media services, including identity labeling and service-provider security obligations.

items.name: Model Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework (Second Edition)
items.scope: Voluntary governance framework for private-sector AI deployment in Singapore, covering internal governance, human-AI decision patterns, operations management, and stakeholder communication. Widely used as an Asia-Pacific procurement baseline.

items.name: Directive on Automated Decision-Making
items.scope: Binding directive for federal government institutions using automated decision systems, including Algorithmic Impact Assessments and transparency duties. Primary vertical is public-sector; listed more broadly because provincial and crown entities often mirror it.

items.name: Conflicts of Interest Relating to the Use of Predictive Data Analytics by Broker-Dealers and Investment Advisers
items.scope: Proposed SEC rulemaking on conflicts when broker-dealers and advisers use predictive data analytics or similar AI technologies that could place firm interests ahead of investors. Finance vertical only; treat as proposed until finalized.

items.name: OCC Comptroller's Handbook: Model Risk Management
items.body: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
items.scope: Supervisory expectations for model risk management at national banks and federal savings associations, including AI/ML models used in credit, BSA/AML, and operations. Complements Fed/FDIC SR 26-2 for the OCC-supervised population.

items.name: FINRA Regulatory Notice 24-09: Artificial Intelligence in the Securities Industry
items.scope: FINRA notice on AI use by member firms, covering supervision, model governance, vendor management, and existing rule obligations that already apply to AI-enabled tools.

items.name: California AB 2013: Generative Artificial Intelligence Training Data Transparency
items.scope: Requires generative AI developers to publish documentation about training-data sources used to create generative AI systems made available to Californians. Subnational transparency duty, not a horizontal AI Act.

items.name: Social Principles of Human-Centric AI
items.scope: Japan's foundational soft-law principles for human-centric AI (dignity, diversity, sustainability). Comparative anchor for Japan's later AI guidelines and AISI work.

items.name: Australia's AI Ethics Principles
items.body: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (Australia)
items.scope: Eight voluntary ethics principles (human wellbeing, human-centred values, fairness, privacy, reliability, transparency, contestability, accountability) used as Australia's national AI soft-law baseline.

items.name: Artificial Intelligence Basic Act (Republic of Korea)
items.body: National Assembly of the Republic of Korea
items.scope: Horizontal national AI statute establishing governance structures, risk-based duties, and transparency obligations. Phased commencement; use as Korea's comparative binding anchor.

items.name: Brazil AI Bill (PL 2338/2023)
items.scope: Proposed Brazilian AI framework bill with risk tiers and rights protections. Reference only until enacted text is stable.

items.name: MeitY Advisories on AI / Generative AI
items.body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (India)
items.scope: Soft-law MeitY advisories on generative AI platforms, due diligence, and user protections. IndiaAI programme companion guidance; no comprehensive AI Act yet.

description: AI regulations and standards mapped to SRF layers and business verticals. The shared catalog is not one-regulation-per-vertical: sector instruments (HIPAA, NAIC, CMMC) apply to one vertical, while cross-cutting instruments (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF) may apply to several. When vertical controls cite an instrument, applicable_verticals is the set of citing verticals (derived-from-controls). When no control cites it yet, authors declare a sector or cross-cutting scope so comparative jurisdiction queries still resolve. Join controls on mapping_key. Jurisdiction ids live in data/jurisdictions.json. Prefer ontology applies_to_vertical edges for agents.
mapping_key_note: Each vertical control's 'mappings' object is keyed by mapping_key. build/generate_knowledge_layer.py turns those into governed_by edges and emits applies_to_vertical edges from applicable_verticals. A mapping_key may be declared before any control cites it, which makes the instrument join-ready: the evidence path stays empty until a control adds a real clause citation under that key. mapping_key stays null for comparative anchors that no control is expected to cite.
vertical_join_note: Control schemas are vertical-specific; this file is a shared instrument catalog. applicable_verticals lists the SRF verticals (finance, healthcare, insurance, public-sector, defense, manufacturing) where the instrument is in scope on this site. Prefer derived-from-controls when mapping_key citations exist. declared-sector is a single-vertical author call. declared-cross-cutting is used only when no control cites the instrument yet and the instrument is horizontal. derived+declared means citations and author scope agree.
